intro_html: A bare crate tray is cold, hard and loud every time they shift. These dog crate beds and travel beds give the crate, the boot and the back seat a soft floor.
description_html:
The crate is often the most-used bed in the house: the whole night, the school run, the hour you're out. A bare tray is cold, hard and loud every time they shift, and a folded blanket ends up in one corner by morning. A dog crate bed is cut to lie flat in that space, so the padding stays under them instead of bunched against the bars.

Dog crate beds, mats and a car seat

Four pieces, each doing a slightly different job:

  • Glenridding: a quilted crate mattress with low padded sides and a zipped cover that washes at 30°C. Small 70 × 50cm, Medium 90 × 60cm, Large 105 × 70cm.
  • Ribble: bolstered sides to lean on, a padded middle and a coated outer that wipes clean after a wet walk. Four sizes, 70 × 55cm to 105 × 75cm.
  • Derwent: a low-profile mat with a coated, wipe-clean surface, in three footprints from 60 × 45cm to 90 × 65cm.
  • Whinlatter: a car seat with around 10cm of memory foam, an inside listed at about 66 × 38cm and a stated limit of about 25kg.

How to choose: crate, boot or back seat

Start with the space, not the dog. Measure the inside of the crate base or the boot floor, then choose the size that lies flat without bunching or blocking the door. A bed that rides up at the edges gives them a ridge to lie on. Then match it to how they rest:

  • If they prop their chin on things: Ribble's bolsters or Glenridding's low padded edge.
  • If they drop and sleep, or come back from every walk soaked: Derwent's flat, wipeable surface.
  • If they ride on the seat rather than in the boot: Whinlatter, checked against its listed inside size and load before you order.

What makes a crate bed work

Fit and surface. It has to reach the edges so the whole floor is padded, and its surface has to survive the drive home from a muddy field. Ribble and Derwent use coated fabric you wipe down; Glenridding's cover unzips for the machine. Check the sewn-in label before washing any coated cover, because detergent can affect some waterproof finishes. For a flat bed for the rest of the house, see our dog mattresses.

And one plain safety line: a bed is a comfort accessory, not a vehicle restraint. Whinlatter is not crash-tested safety equipment, so use a suitable restraint and follow the fitting instructions.

Trying it at home

A crate bed has to earn its place over a few weeks of nights and journeys. Glenridding, Ribble and Derwent come with the 100-night sleep trial: if it isn't right within 100 nights, we arrange free UK mainland collection and a full refund. One trial per household; damage and other exclusions apply. Whinlatter is a travel accessory, so check its returns terms before ordering rather than assuming the trial covers it. Free standard UK delivery on orders over £40.

Crate bed questions

What size dog crate bed do I need?

Measure the inside of the crate base, length and width, and choose the size that matches without folding. If you're torn between two, the one that lies flat beats the one that buckles. The size guide shows how to measure your dog too.

Can I use a crate bed in the car?

Yes, as somewhere comfortable to lie in the boot or a travel crate, alongside a proper restraint. Ribble and Derwent both come in sizes to measure against a boot floor.

Are these crate beds waterproof?

Ribble and Derwent have coated, wipe-clean outers, which handle wet paws and mud between washes. Of the beds in our waterproof dog beds, Wasdale and the Crummock Waterproof Nest are the ones whose fabric is described as waterproof.

Not sure which fits your dog's routine? The Bed Finder asks how they sleep and points you to one bed.
